component.name: Razer Synapse
component.summary: Run Razer Synapse on Linux and configure your Razer devices

description.p: Razer Synapse is Razer's own software for their mice, keyboards and other peripherals. It is Windows-only. This package runs the current Synapse 4 on Linux under a patched build of Wine, talking to your devices directly over HID, the way it does on Windows.
What works, verified with a Naga V2 Pro on its HyperSpeed receiver:

ul.li: The mouse and its receiver are detected, with live battery level
The device's settings are read from it -- sensitivity stages, polling rate, which side plate is fitted
Changes are written back to the mouse, confirmed by reading them back independently
Button assignments apply everywhere on the desktop, through the mouse's own firmware
The interface scales to match your desktop

description.p: Razer Synapse itself is not included. Razer's own installer is downloaded from Razer the first time the application starts, and you install Synapse from it as you would on Windows. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Razer.

One step needs root on the host and cannot be done from inside the sandbox: installing a udev rule so that Razer devices are readable by your user. Run "flatpak run --command=razer-synapse-setup io.github.adds39939.SynapseLinux --udev-help" for the exact commands. If you already use OpenRGB, its rule covers it.
First release. Wine, patched, is bundled -- nothing is needed on the host except a udev rule.
